solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Experienced unease as one dismantled fences

indicators.note: to fence something is to enclose it, so these clue words are read as enclosing the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone felt uneasy as a single ex-bunch of fences was taken apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fences' tells you the answer is enclosed in the run of letters across 'unease as one dismantled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned campaigner or traveller is a practised, veteran one.

clue.text: Film Charlie climbing ridge with others

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about the extraterrestrial
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word for ridge is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an arete is a sharp mountain ridge

explanation.surface: A film shows Charlie scaling a mountain ridge in company with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ARETE, so it is written ETERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera, Latin for 'and the rest', tacks on further unnamed items after a list.

clue.text: One all in purple initially summoned church guards

indicators.note: the summoned-plus-church letters stand around the purple initial, as guards surround what they protect

parts.note: summoned means sent for

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of purple is wanted

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A worshipper dressed in purple was called in by church guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all in' is British for exhausted. 'guards' puts P from 'purple initially' inside SENT FOR + CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spent force is a person or movement whose energy and influence are used up, someone utterly exhausted.

clue.text: Hardly fair upsetting a large number, by Jiminy!

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting turns the large number on its head, so it is read upwards

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred, a large number
Jiminy Cricket is the cricket in Disney's Pinocchio; 'by Jiminy' is also an old exclamation

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims 'by Jiminy!' at an unfairly overturned big score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns TON into NOT. Cricket is the English bat-and-ball game whose fair-play ethos gives the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not cricket' is British idiom for unsporting or dishonourable conduct, so something not cricket is hardly fair.

clue.text: Appreciate one fight that you'd see on TV?

parts.note: to dig something is slang for appreciating it
I is the Roman numeral one
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Do you enjoy a boxing match broadcast on television?
explanation.definitionFit: A digibox was the set-top decoder British viewers used to receive digital television channels.

clue.text: Great display that sees champ finally clean up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for clean is read from the bottom

parts.note: to mop is to clean a floor

indicators.note: finally says to take only the closing letter of champ

explanation.surface: A spectacle in which a champion ends up tidying the arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the cleaning word, as this is a down clue; 'finally' picks the closing letter of 'champ', placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is ceremonial splendour, the magnificent show of a state occasion.

clue.text: Cross when entertaining character at the end repeated gag

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the cross takes the letters inside it

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
Z is the final character of the alphabet
repeated supplies the same final character a second time, beside the first

explanation.surface: Someone angry when a character keeps repeating the same joke at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry' but is the hybrid animal; 'repeated' doubles Z to ZZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A muzzle is a gag, something strapped over the mouth to stop biting or speaking.

clue.text: Old revolutionary's name put up by king before once

parts.note: K is king in chess notation
ere is an old word for before
to sky a ball is to hit it high in the air

explanation.surface: A former rebel's name was raised by a monarch in earlier times.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has', a link. 'by' lets the pieces be read in the order K, ERE, N, SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Kerensky led Russia's provisional government in 1917, before the Bolsheviks seized power.

clue.text: Wellington is smooth, fitting round front of knee

parts.note: to iron cloth is to smooth it

indicators.note: round says the fitting word encircles the letter

parts.note: due means fitting or appropriate

indicators.note: front of says only the first letter of knee is used

explanation.surface: A wellington boot is sleek and fits snugly round the front of the knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' looks like the boot; it is the Duke himself. 'round' puts K inside DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Duke was the nickname of Arthur Wellesley, Duke of Wellington, victor of Waterloo.

clue.text: Maybe grave misfortune, suffering loss of identity

indicators.note: suffering loss of says the identity letters are taken away from the misfortune

parts.note: an accident is a misfortune
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A serious mishap left someone with amnesia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like serious; it is the grave accent, à. 'Maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The grave is one example of a written accent, a mark over a letter like the acute or circumflex.

clue.text: Agree to keep old tank mainly for one of our relatives

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the agreeing word surrounds the tank

parts.note: to chime (in) with is to agree with

indicators.note: mainly says most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Panzer was the German tank of the Second World War

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to look after a vintage tank on behalf of a relation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the tank's last letter, and 'to keep' wraps the agreeing word around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimpanzee is a great ape, humans' closest living kin among animals.

clue.text: Buzzer loud, leading to complaint

parts.note: a bee buzzes, so is a buzzer
f (forte) is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A loud buzzer sets off a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is slang for a grievance or grumble.

clue.text: Image-obsessed female maybe changing a lot into one frock

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: into says the rearranged letters go inside the frock

parts.note: a frock is a dress

indicators.note: changing says the letters of a lot are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vain woman keeps changing in and out of a single frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges 'a lot', and 'into' places the result inside the frock, after the one.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolatress is a woman who worships idols, graven images; 'maybe' flags the play on image.

clue.text: A commercial, alternatively, featuring male singer in rep

indicators.note: featuring means including, so the other pieces hold the male singer

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement, a commercial
or introduces an alternative
a bass is a low-voiced male singer

explanation.surface: A TV advert, or else one with a male singer in a repertory show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rep' looks like repertory theatre; it is short for representative.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a country's official representative abroad.

clue.text: Support resistance with collaborator and some ammunition

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
an ally is a collaborator
a round is one shot's worth of ammunition

explanation.surface: Backing for the Resistance arrives with a helper and some bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally round is to come together to help someone in trouble.

clue.text: Flavouring from wine drink put back into pop

indicators.note: into says the reversed drink goes inside the word for father

parts.note: pop and papa are both words for father

indicators.note: put back says the drink is written in reverse

parts.note: kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: Seasoning comes from a wine cocktail tipped back into fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns KIR into RIK, which goes 'into' PAPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a red spice ground from dried peppers, used to season food.

clue.text: Men of low rank rate mixing with VIPs

indicators.note: mixing says the letters of rate and VIPs are stirred together

explanation.surface: Lowly soldiers rate rubbing shoulders with important people.
explanation.definitionFit: Privates are the lowest-ranking soldiers in an army.

clue.text: Competency rating, one linked with written material, variable

parts.note: a rating is a sailor; AB is an able seaman
I is the Roman numeral one
lit is short for literature
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A competency score for a single text tied to a variable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like a score; in the navy a rating is an ordinary sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ability is the competence or capacity to do something.

clue.text: Farewell party visited by Pope, also earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts the word for also in front of the rest

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: visited by means a guest comes inside, so the Pope goes into the party

parts.note: a do is a party
Leo is the name of many popes

explanation.surface: A goodbye party the Pope also dropped in on beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-oo is a jaunty old British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Maybe not exactly deprive of the lead

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means not plumb, not exactly vertical
as a verb; plumbum is Latin for lead

explanation.definitionFit: Plumb means exactly vertical and comes from Latin plumbum, lead, so un-plumb negates either sense.

clue.text: Body parts, large and small, found in canal

definitions.text: Body parts, large and small, found in canal

parts.words: Body parts, large and small, found in canal
parts.note: the alimentary canal includes the large and small bowel, so 'canal' is not a waterway

explanation.surface: Bodies, big and small, have been fished out of a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canal' suggests a waterway and grim discoveries; it is the alimentary canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The gut is divided into large and small sections, both part of the digestive tract.

clue.text: Yacht: it moves after stopping a minute

indicators.note: moves says the letters of yacht and it are shifted around
after stopping says the a is halted, dropped from the mix before the letters settle

explanation.surface: A yacht starts sailing again after stopping for a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges the letters of the yacht and 'it', while 'after stopping a' takes the A out of that pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is British slang for tiny, very small.

clue.text: Oddly appearing if nobody has returned for the kids, funnily

indicators.note: has returned says the picked letters are read backwards
oddly appearing says only alternate letters of the words show

explanation.surface: Strangely, the kids show up as if nobody came back.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every other letter of 'if nobody' gives FOOY, which 'has returned' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoof is a jokey British spelling of youth, mocking how young people talk.

clue.text: Team's salvation left up in the air

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: up in the air means scattered, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A club's survival in the league is still undecided.
explanation.walkthrough: ASTON VILLA is a Birmingham football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is an English football club, so it is one example of a team.

clue.text: Change your voting system after revolution

indicators.note: after revolution says the pieces have been turned round

parts.note: AV is the alternative vote, a voting system

explanation.surface: Your electoral method changed after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests an uprising; it is the turnaround of YRAV.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary is to alter or change something.

clue.text: Put out note, second-hand

parts.note: do is a note of the sol-fa scale
used means second-hand

explanation.surface: A note is put out, already used.
explanation.definitionFit: To douse a fire or light is to extinguish it.

clue.text: Sounding extremely ecstatic when given appropriate stuff

indicators.note: extremely says only the outermost letters of ecstatic are taken

parts.note: to hog is to take for oneself, appropriate
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Someone sounds thrilled when handed the right stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, to take.
explanation.definitionFit: An echogram is a recording from ultrasonic or echo sounding, as in sonar.

clue.text: New onboard motor's last thing you should hit!

indicators.note: new says the letters are made fresh, arranged differently
last says only the final letter is taken from the motor

explanation.surface: A fresh outboard motor is the last thing a boater wants to collide with.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter is R, last of 'motor'; the 's is 'is'. 'couldn't hit a barn door' mocks a poor shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn door is a proverbially huge target, so anyone should be able to strike it.
